questions.q: How many arguments does ISNULL accept, compared to COALESCE?
options: ISNULL always takes exactly two; COALESCE can take any number
Both take exactly two, always
ISNULL can take any number; COALESCE is limited to two
Both can take any number, with no difference
questions.explain: ISNULL is a strictly two-argument function; COALESCE can chain as many fallback expressions as needed in one call.

questions.q: What determines the result type of ISNULL(expr1, expr2)?
options: Always NVARCHAR(MAX), regardless of the inputs
Standard ANSI data type precedence across both arguments
The declared data type of expr1, the FIRST argument
Whichever argument has the longer declared length
questions.explain: ISNULL's return type comes from its first argument's type, which is exactly what causes the truncation gotcha.

questions.q: Given DECLARE @ShortCode VARCHAR(5) = NULL;, what does ISNULL(@ShortCode, 'This is a much longer fallback string') return?
options: The full string, untruncated
NULL, because @ShortCode is NULL
'This ' — truncated to 5 characters because the result type is VARCHAR(5)
An error, because the types don't match
questions.explain: ISNULL's result is typed VARCHAR(5) from the first argument, so the longer fallback string is silently cut down to fit.

questions.q: Why doesn't COALESCE(@ShortCode, 'This is a much longer fallback string') truncate the same way?
options: COALESCE ignores the first argument's type entirely
COALESCE converts everything to INT first
COALESCE follows ANSI data type precedence across all arguments, producing a result type wide enough for the longer string
COALESCE always returns NVARCHAR(MAX) no matter what
questions.explain: COALESCE's result type is based on data type precedence across every argument, not just the first one, so it sizes to fit the widest value.

questions.q: Which of the two functions is part of the ANSI SQL standard, and portable to other databases?
options: Neither is part of the ANSI standard
Both are ANSI standard
ISNULL — COALESCE is T-SQL-specific to SQL Server
COALESCE — ISNULL is T-SQL-specific to SQL Server
questions.explain: COALESCE is ANSI-standard SQL; ISNULL is a SQL Server-only function (other platforms use NVL, IFNULL, etc.).
